question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,0]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-1 \\ {x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}-2\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-1.5,\,1]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{2}≈[$ {{field-1}} $]$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x & -2y \\ 3{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2} & -6xy\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & -2y \\ 3{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2} & -6xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-1 \\ {x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & -2y \\ 3{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2} & -6xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-1 \\ {x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(-1.5) & -2(1) \\ 3(-1.5)^{2}-3(1)^{2} & -6(-1.5)(1)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-1.5)^{2}-(1)^{2}-1 \\ (-1.5)^{3}-3(-1.5)(1)^{2}-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 3.75 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0.25 \\ -0.875\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-3)\cdot 9-(-2)\cdot 3.75}[\begin{aligned}9 & 2 \\ -3.75 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0.25 \\ -0.875\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{19.5}[\begin{aligned}0.5 \\ 1.6875\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-1.474 \\ 1.087\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
